lesson.title: Updating 2D List Cells
lesson.driving_question: How can a program update one field without replacing the whole record?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Replacing one field in a selected 2D-list row
lesson.concept_budget: Replace one valid cell using a row index and a fixed field index; row editing and validation are deferred.
misconceptions: Double-index assignment changes one cell only.
The outer index still selects the row.
The field index must match the intended column.
A numeric field should receive a numeric value.
lesson.progression_note: Extends the reading model from Lesson 28 to controlled updates of individual fields.

shared_program.code:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
row = int(input("Club row 0 to 2: "))
new_members = int(input("New member count: "))
clubs[row][1] = new_members
print("Updated record:", clubs[row])
print("All records:", clubs)

primm.prompt: Recall how index assignment replaces one item in a 1D list and how two indexes identify a 2D-list cell.
Use row 1 and 20. Mark the one changed cell and list every value that remains unchanged.
Run with 1 and 20, then restart with 0 and 10. Confirm that only the selected member count changes.

questions: Which of the two indexes selects the row, and which selects the field to update?
Why does clubs[row][1] = new_members leave the club name unchanged?
What happens if new_members is not converted to int() before it is stored?
How could choosing the wrong column silently replace a name with a number?

primm.prompt: Change the program so the second input is a number of members to add, not a replacement total. Add it to the selected row's existing member count. Test row 2 and 2 new members; Code must become 17 and all other records must remain unchanged.

Ask for a row from 0 to 2 and store it in [row]. Display "Before:" followed by [clubs][row]. Ask for a new club name and member count and store them in [new_name] and [new_members]. Update both cells in the selected row, then display "After:" followed by the updated row. Test row 1, "Robotics" and 22; display "Before: ['Chess', 18]" and "After: ['Robotics', 22]".

Store the rows ['Pens', 10], ['Books', 6] and ['Tape', 4] in [stock]. Ask for a row from 0 to 2 and store it in [row]. Ask for a delivery amount and store it in [delivery], then add [delivery] to the quantity at [stock][row][1]. Display the updated row followed by every item name and quantity. Test row 2 and delivery 3; the updated row must be ['Tape', 7].
Repair the double-index assignment and convert the new member count to an integer.

programs.challenge1:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
row = int(input("Club row 0 to 2: "))
members_to_add = int(input("Members to add: "))

clubs[row][1] = clubs[row][1] + members_to_add

print("Updated record:", clubs[row])
print("All records:", clubs)
programs.challenge2:
clubs = [["Art", 12], ["Chess", 18], ["Code", 15]]
row = int(input("Club row 0 to 2: "))
print("Before:", clubs[row])
new_name = input("New club name: ")
new_members = int(input("New member count: "))
clubs[row][0] = new_name
clubs[row][1] = new_members
print("After:", clubs[row])
programs.challenge3:
stock = [["Pens", 10], ["Books", 6], ["Tape", 4]]
row = int(input("Stock row 0 to 2: "))
delivery = int(input("Delivery amount: "))
sold = int(input("Number sold: "))
stock[row][1] = stock[row][1] + delivery - sold
print("Updated record:", stock[row])
for item in stock:
    print(item[0], item[1])
